Name: Primary
Description: Controls the main weathering effect, which adds lighter coloration to the sharpest protrusions and exposed areas of the terrain, simulating the effect of sun-bleached or eroded surfaces.

Name: Scale
Description: Sets the scale at which weathering effects are applied. Lower values target fine details, while higher values affect larger terrain features.

Name: Creep
Description: Simulates gradual movement and spreading of weathering effects across the terrain, softening transitions and blending weathered areas.

Name: Amount
Description: Adjusts the overall intensity of the weathering effect. Higher values produce more pronounced weathering.

Name: Washed Out
Description: Toggles if colors are faded or desaturated, mimicking the effect of prolonged exposure to the elements.

Name: Inverse
Description: Inverts the weathering effect, applying it to areas that would normally be less affected, such as recesses instead of protrusions.

Name: Dirt
Description: Adds darker coloration to crevices, nooks, and sheltered areas of the terrain, simulating the accumulation of soil, organic matter, or moisture.

Name: Darker
Description: Intensifies the darkness of the dirt effect, making crevices and nooks appear deeper and more shadowed.

Name: Post Processing
Description: Contains controls for final color adjustments after weathering has been applied.

Name: Hue
Description: Adjusts the overall hue of the weathered terrain, allowing for color shifts to match desired environmental conditions.

Name: Saturation
Description: Controls the intensity of colors in the weathered terrain, from muted to vibrant.

Name: Lightness
Description: Sets the overall brightness of the weathered terrain, affecting how light or dark the final result appears.
